text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The accord signed by miners' union leaders with the government on Friday is decisive for mining restructuring, the newspaper says.
- Managers of the Cluj-based heating systems maker Termorom say that the plant, on the list of 17 state-owned companies slated for closure, would have come out of the red in one year.
- "A banker is responsible for the credits he gives," Romanian banks association president Constantin Duna says in interview.
- Five foreign bidders have offered more than the minimum price of $216 million asked by the State Ownership Fund for the sale of the Petromidia oil refinery, the newspaper says.
- On September 1, the Romtelecom telephone authority will become Romania's first utility, due for privatisation, created from a state-owned "regie autonome", says newspaper report.
- Local authorities in the Transyolvanian city of Sibiu plan to put the local job exchange on the Internet communications superhighway.
- The newspaper prints a statement issued by the government on the procedures for winding up state companies which have run up chronic debts.
- Police are searching for two men who staged an armed robbery at the Baneasa petrol station near Bucharest before dawn on Sunday, the newspaper says.
- "God was with me throughout the race," Gabriela Szabo, winner of the gold medal in the women's 5,000 metre race in Athens world athletics championships, says in interview.
- Around 40,000 immigrants from various Arab countries have settled in a district in the Western city of Timisoara, dubbed the "Gaza Strip" by local residents, a newspaper report says.
- Some 400 inmates at the Gherla jail say local jail authorities compel them to work as slaves in a local furniture factory, says newspaper report.

- Authorities in southwest Ukraine and northern Romania have signed an accord to build the first road bridge over the Tisa river bordering the two countries, the newspaper says. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
